question:
(i) An ideal LC circuit has inductance $L$ and capacitance $C$. Write the expression for its frequency of oscillation.
(ii) How will the frequency change if the capacitance is made four times its initial value, keeping inductance unchanged?
(iii) How will the frequency change if the inductance is made nine times its initial value, keeping capacitance unchanged? Justify your answers.

options.A:
(i) $f=2\pi\sqrt{LC}$.
(ii) If $C$ becomes $4C$, frequency becomes double.
(iii) If $L$ becomes $9L$, frequency becomes three times.
options.B:
(i) $f=\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$.
(ii) If $C$ becomes $4C$, frequency becomes $\frac{f}{2}$.
(iii) If $L$ becomes $9L$, frequency becomes $\frac{f}{3}$, since $f\propto\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$.
options.C:
(i) $f=\frac{1}{LC}$.
(ii) If $C$ becomes $4C$, frequency becomes $\frac{f}{4}$.
(iii) If $L$ becomes $9L$, frequency becomes $\frac{f}{9}$.
options.D:
(i) $f=\frac{1}{2\pi LC}$.
(ii) Changing capacitance does not affect frequency.
(iii) Changing inductance does not affect frequency.
